clue.text: One may be suspended for relaxing

definitions.text: One may be suspended for relaxing

parts.words: One may be suspended for relaxing
parts.note: 'suspended' hints at punishment, but here it is literal: a bed of netting hung between two supports to lounge in

explanation.surface: Someone caught taking it easy at work may be suspended from the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A netting bed slung between trees or posts is hung up, and people lie in it to rest.

clue.text: Notice pair with enough

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
to pair things is to equate them, treating them as matching

explanation.surface: A notice that pairs up with enough of something, like a sufficient advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is sufficient, meeting the need without surplus.

clue.text: Feel the loss of our island state

parts.note: to miss someone is to feel the loss of them
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An islander laments losing their homeland, which is also their state.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Wow! A coin up for exchange, that's riches indeed

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow

indicators.note: a coin offered for exchange is swapped about, so these letters are traded into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a coin being handed over in exchange, as if it were a great fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wow!' looks like the clue's opening exclamation, but it is the British cry 'cor' doing a job in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia, the horn of plenty, stands for overflowing abundance and wealth.

clue.text: Devise a scheme that's ordinary without one

indicators.note: 'without one' says the plain word must go without its numeral for one

parts.note: plain means ordinary or unadorned
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Advice that a scheme is only ordinary if it lacks a single key element.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan is to work out a scheme or arrangement in advance.

clue.text: Open with nothing to replace a pin

indicators.note: 'with nothing to replace a' tells us the circle for nothing takes the place of the letter a

parts.note: to broach a subject or a cask is to open it
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening something with no tool other than a substitute for a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' looks like an article before 'pin', but it is the letter A in BROACH that O replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is an ornamental clasp fastened to clothing with a pin.

clue.text: Uniform worn by American partner in the normal course of events

definitions.text: in the normal course of events

indicators.note: clothes worn by someone are on them, so the letter for uniform is held within the other pieces

parts.note: an ally is a partner
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American's partner routinely wears a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually means as a rule, what generally happens day to day.

clue.text: Warm heart (mostly) and face

indicators.note: 'mostly' signals that the word for heart loses its final letter

parts.note: the core of something is its heart
dial is slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: A description of someone with a warm heart, mostly, and a friendly face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial greeting is friendly and genial in manner.

clue.text: A source of light — and forces panicked outside

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of light

indicators.note: panicked troops scatter in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A light source appears and the armed forces panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, as in eating outdoors.

clue.text: Criticise Conservative guarantee

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the British political party
to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A Tory demands to criticise a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure is to rebuke or condemn formally.

clue.text: Inappropriate and drawn out, after a fashion

indicators.note: done after a fashion means done loosely, so the letters are rearranged loosely too

explanation.surface: Something both improper and long-winded, done only half well.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unseemly or unexpected in an unwelcome way.

clue.text: General shift in values surrounding Republican

indicators.note: 'surrounding' has the shifted letters go around the letter for Republican
a shift is a change of position, so these letters move around

explanation.surface: A political note about a broad change of values hemming in a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to all cases, so widespread or across the board.

clue.text: Puzzle of party held by partners in special relationship going west

indicators.note: a party held by the partners sits between them
in an across answer going west means travelling right to left, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: the 'special relationship' is the UK and US alliance, so the partners are UK and US
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a party hosted jointly by Britain and America as they head west.
explanation.walkthrough: UK + US read backwards gives SUKU, and DO goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placing logic puzzle on a nine-by-nine grid.

clue.text: Furry animal may be cold in far-eastern country

indicators.note: the word for cold goes in the country's name

parts.note: China is a country in the Far East
a chill is a cold, or chill means cold

explanation.surface: A furry animal might feel cold in China.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a small South American rodent prized for its very soft, dense coat.

clue.text: Disappointed after Derby tip, perhaps

parts.note: a punter whose tip for the Derby horse race loses is fed up; Derby is also a kind of English cheese

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, and Derby is also a hard cheese, which is the wink at the slang word for being fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for annoyed, fed up or let down.

clue.text: Wake up cooler?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rouse or awaken
second meaning: cooler is slang for prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' reads like a fridge or a cooler day, but both it and the answer are slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to rouse from sleep and, in slang, a prison cell or jail.

clue.text: Simple men thinking about tool

indicators.note: the answer is found about, or within, the phrase, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: Simple-minded men pondering a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it signals the answer sits in the run of letters, from the second letter of 'Simple' to the first of 'thinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a tool or utensil used for a particular job.

clue.text: Measure of warmth there after renovating stable

parts.note: a tog is a unit measuring the warmth of a duvet or clothing

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds something, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note on warmth in a stable after it was renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: The tog is the British rating for how warm a duvet is; 'stable' reads as a horse's building but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is together is emotionally steady and well-organised.

clue.text: Tobacco plant that's a creeper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a type of tobacco, from the US state
second meaning: the ... creeper is a climbing plant, and the question mark flags that the word alone stands for it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tobacco plant creeping along; Virginia names a tobacco leaf and, with 'creeper', a climbing vine.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is both a tobacco variety and the first word of a common climbing vine's name.

clue.text: Notice vehicle protected by youth under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under means following below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sign about a car looked after by a young man who is under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a posted notice or sign, often carried at protests.

clue.text: Make economies? That's no good

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make economies is to ..., read as two words
second meaning: of no use or value

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first sense splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the word means worthless; split in two, it means consuming a smaller amount.

clue.text: State origins of open hostility in Oxford

indicators.note: the origins of words are their beginnings, their first letters

explanation.surface: A report of open hostility breaking out in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is a US state in the Midwest, bordering Lake Erie.

clue.text: Fruitless campaigns having mislaid bags outside university

parts.note: something mislaid is lost

indicators.note: the cases sit outside, wrapping round the letter for university

parts.note: cases are bags or luggage

explanation.surface: Students whose campaigns failed after their bags went missing outside a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost causes are efforts with no hope of success.

clue.text: Target identified among America's troublemakers?

indicators.note: the answer is identified among the letters, spanning the words

explanation.surface: A target named in a list of those America viewed as troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'America's' into 'troublemakers'. Fidel Castro was the Cuban leader the US repeatedly tried to topple.
explanation.definitionFit: Castro was a notorious target of American assassination plots during the Cold War.

clue.text: Go green, after cooking with yoghurt initially

indicators.note: food after cooking is transformed, so these letters are rearranged
initially means the first letter

parts.note: first letter of yoghurt

explanation.surface: A health-food recipe: go green by cooking with yoghurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning drive or vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Go here is a noun meaning vigour or drive, as in full of get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Enormous deficit in fossil fuel

indicators.note: the deficit word goes in the fuel word

parts.note: coal is a fossil fuel
a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: A news report of a huge shortfall in fossil fuel supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge, like the giant statue the Colossus.

clue.text: Top answer with Times supporting exercise

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath, so the letter for times goes below the one for exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A top answer in The Times, backing a form of exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' places X beneath PE in this down answer, so X comes last; the capital on 'Times' suggests the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Heartless Nero has obsession that's trivial

definitions.note: noun 'a nothing', something trivial, used here adjectivally

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters are removed from Nero

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

explanation.surface: The cruel emperor Nero has a fixation that amounts to little.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing can describe something of no importance, as in a nothing remark.

clue.text: Shy engineers had their uses

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
things that served have had their uses

explanation.surface: Bashful engineers were nevertheless useful.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is restrained and reticent, slow to open up.

clue.text: Capability of a Ford designed for work on the farm?

definitions.text: Capability of a Ford designed for work on the farm?

indicators.note: a vehicle designed anew is rearranged, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A Ford vehicle built for farm work must handle rough ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-road capability means driving across fields and tracks away from paved highways.
